name: Fofie

card.sum: A yam festival of thanks for the harvest, ending in a durbar of chiefs carried through the streets.

metaDescription: Fofie is a yam festival held in October in Techiman and at Nchiraa near Wenchi in the Bono East Region: thanks for the harvest and a durbar of chiefs. What we know and tips.
ogTitle: Fofie: the yam festival of Techiman
subtitle: Thanks for the yam harvest
answer: Fofie is a yam festival held in October in the Bono East Region. In Techiman it is known as Fofie Kesee and gives thanks to God and the ancestors for a good yam harvest, the area’s main staple, ending in a durbar with the paramount chief carried in a palanquin through the streets. It is also kept at Nchiraa, near Wenchi.

sections.title: What we know
sections.html:
The yam festival honours and thanks God and the ancestors for a high yam yield, the main staple of the area. In Techiman the chiefs, with the paramount chief in a palanquin, parade through the main streets to a durbar.[[2]] The chiefs and people of Nchiraa near Wenchi also celebrate Fofie each October.[[1]]

We haven’t found a clear account of how Fofie began, or whether the Techiman and Nchiraa celebrations share one history. If you know, tell us.

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Techiman is a busy market town on the road north from Kumasi.
Check the dates: the traditional council sets the days each year, often only weeks ahead. Local radio and the national press carry the announcement.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
Also in Techiman: Apoo, the festival of speaking out.
